title: the next gate read cannot be a measurement: 1 post-intervention post(s) can carry insights inside the 09-28 13:00 review window (need 5) while the render loop is refused
evidence: next weekly review 09-28 13:00Z; its window is [(review - 7d), review]. Post-intervention pool (photos rendered at/after 2026-09-21 23:35:00Z -- the content-mix lever, inside Growth::GateRead::INTERVENTION_AT): 7. Inside that window the SLOTS hold 0 published + 4 queued = 4, but Growth::GateRead#cohort_size ALSO requires insights_updated_at, and insights arrive a measured 24h after publication (fastest observed publish->insights lag, taken from the DB) -- so a slot inside the window's last 24h can never testify. FEASIBLE cohort: 0 published + 1 queued = 1, against MIN_COHORT_POSTS=5. Below it Growth::GateRead returns :extend ("re-read, do NOT act") regardless of the date, so the pre-registered GO/PIVOT/KILL read is deferred by arithmetic, not by waiting. Render loop: 12 refusal(s) in the last 12h, so no new post-intervention photo can enter the pool -- the cohort is fed only by renders (publication lags them by the queue depth). That is why a GPU refusal starves the STRATEGY decision and not merely a render window; the :8188 instance (pid 553489, holder operator) was launched WITHOUT --reserve-vram, so `ensure` refuses on the ARGS before it ever asks the scheduler for a claim — this refusal is about the launch line, not about how much VRAM is free (see COMFY_RESERVE_VRAM). Response: the OPERATOR's interactive session -- a human is using the shared install; yield the window, do not touch/restart/re-flag it (a running process's args are not ours to change). Nothing here is ours to repair -- the refusal itself is correct (an instance launched without --reserve-vram cannot be submitted to) -- and this entry is not an ask on the holder: it self-closes when the loop stops being refused.
